findings.reason: The protected Python solution determines if a number string is strobogrammatic using a two-pointer approach, comparing symmetric pairs of characters using a 180-degree rotation lookup dictionary. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.
A 180-degree rotation inverts position order and maps 0, 1, 8 to themselves, and 6 to 9. Checking all symmetric character pairs against the rotation map proves or disproves strobogrammatic symmetry.

The two-pointer loop performs n / 2 character lookups and comparisons, running in O(n) time and using O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed 5-pair dictionary. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts string num, returning a boolean indicating whether num is a strobogrammatic number.

The approach accurately details 180-degree rotation digit pairs, two-pointer inward scanning, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover full-string rotation allocation, invalid digit rejection, and middle-digit self-symmetry rules for odd-length inputs.
